image_description: A close-up macro shot of a brown butterfly, identified as a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), perched on a green leaf. The wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is characterized by a uniform brown color and a row of distinct eyespots (ocelli) with yellow rings and black centers along the hindwing margin. The background is a soft, out-of-focus green.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wing coloration is a consistent earthy brown. A clear row of ocelli is visible on the hindwing, matching the diagnostic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo and the position of the legs against the leaf make it impossible to distinguish the reduced forelegs from the other legs or the substrate.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The fringe scales (cilia) along the very edge of the wing appear slightly smudged or 'melted' into the background in the lower-left quadrant, lacking the crisp individual definition seen in high-quality macro photography.
The tarsi (feet) of the butterfly do not have clear contact points with the leaf surface; they appear to float slightly or merge ambiguously with the leaf texture, lacking precise occlusion shadows.
